claims.text: HEA bond coats produced by atmospheric plasma spraying have relatively high porosity.
HEA bond coats produced by traditional thermal spraying have less optimal interfacial adhesion.
HVOF deposition of HEA bond coats produces a denser, less porous interface than conventional deposition.
Cold-spray deposition of HEA bond coats produces a denser, less porous interface than conventional deposition.
HVOF or cold-spray deposition improves bonding between the HEA bond coat and the substrate.
HVOF and cold spray provide increased particle velocity relative to conventional deposition methods.
Increased particle velocity enhances particle deformation at impact.
Increased particle velocity enhances particle bonding at impact.
Enhanced deformation and impact bonding reduce coating porosity.
Reduced coating porosity minimizes pathways for oxidation during thermal cycling.
Reduced coating porosity minimizes pathways for crack propagation during thermal cycling.
HVOF- or cold-sprayed HEA bond coats will have longer thermal-cycling lifetimes than conventionally deposited HEA bond coats.
HVOF- or cold-sprayed HEA bond coats will resist cracking better than conventionally deposited HEA bond coats.
HVOF- or cold-sprayed HEA bond coats will resist delamination better than conventionally deposited HEA bond coats.
The predicted improvement depends on optimizing particle velocity, temperature, and spray distance for the specific HEA composition.
The predicted improvement depends on substrate roughness and pretreatment remaining within conventional thermal-spray preparation thresholds.
